newsitem.title: USA: BLM launches study of Alaska reserve oil leasing. [CORRECTED 04:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BLM launches study of Alaska reserve oil leasing. [CORRECTED 04:15 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. Bureau of Land Management said Wednesday it will launch a study into new oil development in a federal reserve on Alaska's North Slope.

The agency said within 18 months it will complete an environmental impact statement and activity plan for oil leasing in the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska, a 23 million-acre federal land holding west of the supergiant Prudhoe Bay oil field.

"BLM will seek information and comments from a wide variety of people and organizations, including Alaska Natives, environmental organizations, government groups and other interested parties through an extensive scoping process," BLM Alaska State Director Tom Allen said in a news release.
The Indiana-sized petroleum reserve, established in 1923 by President Warren Harding, could hold 5.5 billion barrels of recoverable oil, according to federal and state estimates.

The petroleum reserve was explored in the past, most extensively in the decade after World War II. Although some oil and gas was discovered, there were no strikes considered to be of commercial quantity.
The last oil and gas leases in the reserve were sold by the federal government in the early 1980s, but oil companies declined to drill there and their leases were relinquished.
The reserve was largely neglected by oil companies until recently. New interest in the area has been spurred by the recent oil discovery on the reserve's eastern edge.
The Alpine field, estimated to hold 250 million to 300 million recoverable barrels, was discovered by Arco Alaska Inc. and partners Anadarko Petroleum and Union Texas Petroleum.
Gov. Tony Knowles, who has promoted new oil development in the reserve, welcomed BLM's announcement.
Knowles, a Democrat, last week secured a promise from Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt to move forward with a leasing study.

"I'm pleased Secretary Babbitt is delivering on his commitment to me and all Alaskans to undertake a thorough effort which I'm confident will lead to an oil lease sale in this potentially oil-rich petroleum reserve," Knowles said.
BLM said its plans for studying oil and gas development in the petroleum reserve will be detailed in Thursday's Federal Register.
Only the northeast corner of the petroleum reserve -- the area adjacent to the new Alpine discovery -- will be considered for oil and gas leasing, BLM said.
Environmentalists have expressed concerns about certain sections of the reserve that are important to migrating waterfowl, calving caribou and other wildlife.
